public_rationale: Screen International reported on May 15, 2024 that The Last Screenwriter was filmed in January 2024 and credited ChatGPT with screenwriting [e1]. The film is a potential replacement example, but the report does not independently establish that it meets the contract's professional replacement standard [e1]. On June 18, 2026, Brian Grazer described using Claude for outlines before handing them to a human writer [e2]. His account establishes continued human involvement in that workflow, not a general inability to replace writers [e2]. Neither report establishes a replacement event whose status and timing meet the contract's early-resolution rule [e1][e2].
limitations: “For some time” specifies no minimum duration or deadline, so elapsed time alone cannot settle the forecast.
The film report relies on the director's account of his contributions and the script's quality [e1].
Neither report establishes replacement of all functions of a writers' room [e1][e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI will not be able to realistically replace a writer or a writers' room for some time.

statement.excerpt: AI isn’t currently at a place (nor do I believe it will be for some time) where it could realistically replace a writer or writer’s room

from_speaker: nor do I believe it will be for some time
realistically replace a writer or writer’s room
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns professional Hollywood screenwriting, including an equivalent professional production elsewhere.
Replacement means performing substantive writing without substantial human writing or rewriting; ordinary direction and editing remain permissible.
For some time supplies neither a deadline nor a minimum duration. I do not substitute a fixed number of years.
criteria.support_condition: A defined minimum interval would have to pass with adequate evidence that realistic replacement remained unavailable. Without such an interval, elapsed time alone cannot settle the forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A verified replacement event occurs at a time that unambiguously conflicts with the predicted continuing inability. A later event alone cannot establish that conflict when the minimum interval is unspecified.

evidence.explanation: The report dates filming to January 2024 and describes an AI-generated screenplay developed through repeated prompts, with scenes and repetitive dialogue cut by the director. This is a substantial replacement candidate, but it does not establish professional equivalence or resolve the unspecified duration.

evidence.locator: Brian Grazer's remarks near the beginning of the article
evidence.explanation: Grazer described using Claude to develop outlines before handing them to a writer. This documents continued human involvement in one professional workflow, not a general technical inability to replace writers.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence establishing the intended minimum interval, plus either a verified professional replacement that unambiguously conflicts with it or adequate evidence that replacement remained unavailable throughout it. Any replacement record must document the date, system, writing duties, human contributions and usability.
